chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the captive whom the polytheists imprison, so the prayer time presents itself, but the one who imprisoned him prevents him from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He indicates by gestures.'

key_terms.الْمُشْرِكُونَ: The polytheists (specifically in the context of early Islamic conflicts)

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim prisoner perform prayer if their captors prevent them from standing or prostrating?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Sumanah illustrates the principle of *darar* (constraint) in Shia jurisprudence, where physical limitation dictates the form of worship. It establishes that when a captive is physically prevented from performing the full postures of prayer, the obligation is fulfilled through minimal gestures (*i'nam*), reflecting the Quranic maxim that God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Zur’at who said,

‘I asked himasws about the captive imprisoned by the Polytheists. So the Salāt (time) presents itself, but the one who imprisoned him prevents him from it. Heasws said: ‘He would indicate by gestures’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from his father from Zur’ah from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is a captive of the pagans. It becomes time for Salah (prayer) and they do not allow him to perform Salah (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ‘He makes gestures as gestures are made.”’
